I’ve had consistently positive experiences with them over the years and truly appreciate the care they provide.

However, I feel it’s important to highlight one recurring issue: the practice manager, Unfortunately, she comes across as condescending and speaks to patients in a way that feels dismissive and rude. It’s disappointing, especially in an environment where empathy and communication are so important. I’ve noticed other reviews mention similar concerns, which makes me feel this is not an isolated incident. Almost acts like a body guard for appointments and depending on her mood will speak to you in a manner that suits her. She’s made us feel uncomfortable calling the surgery on many occasions and when you’re unwell it’s not a pleasant experience. It lets the whole reputation of the surgery down.

I’ve submitted this feedback anonymously because I value my place at the surgery and don’t want it affected. I strongly urge the doctors or whoever is responsible for oversight to look into this matter. Perhaps a mystery shopper or anonymous feedback system could help management better understand what patients are experiencing.

Other than this issue, the surgery is excellent — it would be a perfect 5 stars if the manager showed the same level of compassion and respect as the rest of the team.

Edited Follow-up Review:
It’s quite telling that rather than reflecting on patient feedback, the person replying  has chosen to respond in such a defensive and condescending way — which rather proves my point about the attitude in question.

To clarify, this was not a complaint, but an honest review of my experience as a patient — which is exactly what reviews are for. Suggesting that I “raise a complaint” only reinforces the impression that patient voices are dismissed unless they follow a process the practice can control.

It’s a real shame, because the doctors, nurses, and the majority of the reception team are genuinely excellent — Callum, Victoria, and Karen in particular are always kind, professional, and a huge asset to the surgery. Their approach is everything a patient-facing role should be.

I sincerely hope the partners take the time to read reviews like this and consider how these responses reflect on the wider patient experience. As an NHS professional of nearly ten years, I have found some of this surgery's actions quite disturbing.

I will not go into the character of the practice manager, as there are already many accurate reviews below. What I will say, however, is that she has absolutely no place being anywhere near healthcare.

She was caught on a recorded call fabricating NHS policies to justify discriminatory actions, becoming confrontational, and interrogating a carer for no reason while laughing and mocking her.

The recording was forwarded to the head doctors for a fair investigation. However, they tried to justify her every action. They claimed that laughing over the phone is "de-escalatory"—a notion which is absolutely mind-boggling.

Given the many similar reviews regarding the poor handling (or lack thereof) of complaints, I would like to outline the steps you can take if you are unsatisfied with the surgery's response:

1. Request Recordings: All calls are recorded. You are legally entitled to request a copy through a Subject Access Request (SAR). Do not accept being spoken to like a second-class citizen. Question every NHS policy the manager cites and research them yourself.
2. Escalate Your Complaint: Once you have received a final response from the surgery, escalate your complaint to the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman.
3. Report to the GMC: Report the head doctor(s) who 'investigated' the complaint to the General Medical Council (GMC). They have a duty to resolve complaints with some integrity and objectivity, not blindly defend staff and enable behaviour that is detrimental to public health.
4. Protect Yourself: If you make a complaint, ensure you protect yourself. Log everything and request copies of all recordings and notes. If the manager is capable of creating a fake letter and backdating it to cover her tracks, one can only imagine what else she is capable of.
I retain all evidence, including the voice recording and subsequent correspondence.
